chunks: He said: Regarding a man who prayed one rak‘ah of the Fajr prayer, then went away and came back after morning had come, and remembered that he had prayed only one rak‘ah, he said: “He adds another rak‘ah to it.”

So there is nothing in these reports that contradicts what we have mentioned, because it is not apparent in these reports that the forgetfulness occurred in the supererogatory prayer or the obligatory prayer. They only mention the Fajr prayer and the Maghrib prayer, and it is possible that what is meant by them is the supererogatory prayers, because supererogatory prayers may be ascribed to Fajr, and likewise the supererogatory prayers of Maghrib are ascribed to Maghrib just as the obligatory prayer is ascribed to it. If what we have said is possible, we interpret them in a way such that the reports do not contradict one another.

The first two reports may also bear another meaning, which is that one who doubts in Fajr and Maghrib, but the greater number becomes predominant in his estimation, may therefore build upon it, because predominance of conjecture takes the place of knowledge, as we have explained previously. Even if the slightest doubt still occurs to him along with this, it has no legal effect. Thus his statement, peace be upon him, “He adds another rak‘ah to it,” would be from the standpoint of precaution and recommendation, not obligation and requirement.
And that which indicates this is what he narrated:
And from him, from al-Ḥajjāl, from ʿAbd Allāh, from ʿUbayd, from Abī ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام, who said:

key_terms.السَّهْوَ: forgetfulness or inadvertent error in prayer
key_terms.النَّافِلَةِ: supererogatory prayer, as distinct from the obligatory prayer
key_terms.الِاسْتِظْهَارِ: acting with precaution to ensure correctness
key_terms.الْعِلْمِ: certainty or knowledge in legal determination
key_terms.غَلَبَةَ الظَّنِّ: predominant probability that functions as a practical basis for action

ai.seo_question: How do Shia hadith scholars reconcile reports about doubt in the Fajr and Maghrib prayers?
ai.summary: This passage discusses reports concerning doubt or omission in the Fajr and Maghrib prayers and explains how they may be reconciled without contradiction. It presents the possibility that the reports refer either to supererogatory prayers or to cases where predominant probability is treated like knowledge, making the addition of a rak‘ah a matter of precaution and recommendation rather than obligation.
